subject: plotting maps with insets and projections

messages.author: 6a3b777d6a18967b
messages.subject: plotting maps with insets and projections
parts:
Last year I posted a question about using custom_annotation to make a make of the US with Alaska and Hawaii as insets. That solution worked well for me, but I have started to receive complaints because the map use cartesian coordinates instead of, say, a Mercator projection. However, when I try to add a Mercator projection with coord_map() I get the error:

Error: annotation_custom only works with Cartesian coordinates

Is there something analogous to annotation_custom that I can use for this instead? For reference, I am attaching code that makes the attached map. At the bottom of the code is the attempt to use annotation_custom with projections.

library(choroplethrMaps)
library(choroplethr)
library(ggplot2)
library(mapproj)
library(grid)

theme_clean = function()
{
  theme(
    axis.title        = element_blank(),
    axis.text         = element_blank(),
    panel.background  = element_blank(),
    panel.grid        = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.length = unit(0, "cm"),
    axis.ticks.margin = unit(0, "cm"),
    panel.margin      = unit(0, "lines"),
    plot.margin       = unit(c(0, 0, 0, 0), "lines"),
    complete          = TRUE
  )
}

# like theme clean, but also remove the legend
theme_inset = function()
{
  theme(
    legend.position   = "none",
    axis.title        = element_blank(),
    axis.text         = element_blank(),
    panel.background  = element_blank(),
    panel.grid        = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.length = unit(0, "cm"),
    axis.ticks.margin = unit(0, "cm"),
    panel.margin      = unit(0, "lines"),
    plot.margin       = unit(c(0, 0, 0, 0), "lines"),
    complete          = TRUE
  )
}

data("state.map")

# separate contiguous states from Alaska and Hawaii
us.states.48 = state.map[!state.map$region %in% c("alaska", "hawaii"), ]
alaska.df = state.map[state.map$region=='alaska',]
hawaii.df = state.map[state.map$region=='hawaii',]

# render the lower 48
base = ggplot(us.states.48, aes(long, lat, group=group)) + 
  geom_polygon() +
  theme_clean() 

# render Alaska as a grob, so we can add it as an inset with annotation_custom
alaska.ggplot = ggplot(alaska.df, aes(long, lat, group=group)) + geom_polygon() + theme_inset() + coord_map()
alaska.grob = ggplotGrob(alaska.ggplot)

# render Hawaii as a grob, so we can add it as an inset with annotation_custom
hawaii.ggplot = ggplot(hawaii.df, aes(long, lat, group=group)) + geom_polygon() + theme_inset() + coord_map()
hawaii.grob = ggplotGrob(hawaii.ggplot)

base +
  annotation_custom(grobTree(alaska.grob), xmin=-125, xmax=-110, ymin=22.5, ymax=30) +
  annotation_custom(grobTree(hawaii.grob), xmin=-107.5, xmax=-102.5, ymin=25, ymax=27.5) 

# try to render them all with a mercator projection
# add the projection to each
base = base + coord_map()
alaska.ggplot = alaska.ggplot + coord_map()
alaska.grob = ggplotGrob(alaska.ggplot)
hawaii.ggplot = hawaii.ggplot + coord_map()
hawaii.grob = ggplotGrob(hawaii.ggplot)

# now render
# Error: annotation_custom only works with Cartesian coordinates
base +
  annotation_custom(grobTree(alaska.grob), xmin=-125, xmax=-110, ymin=22.5, ymax=30) +
  annotation_custom(grobTree(hawaii.grob), xmin=-107.5, xmax=-102.5, ymin=25, ymax=27.5)

messages.subject: Re: plotting maps with insets and projections
parts:
Quick update: via twitter Hadley suggested looking at coord_quickmap(). I don't have a good explanation as to why, but this code:

library(choroplethr)
library(ggplot2)

data(df_pop_state)

state_choropleth(df_pop_state)
state_choropleth(df_pop_state) + coord_quickmap()

gives a projection without triggering the custom_annotation error that "+ coord_map()" does. I'm going to incorporate this into the next version of choroplethr.

messages.subject: Re: plotting maps with insets and projections
parts:
that solves some of the problems for some regions (I played with that
a bit in a fork of choroplethr), but not the lack of albers for Russia
and the U.S.

_Still_ having a faux-Mercator that doesn't force folks to precisely
tweak graphics window proportions or graphics device width/height
options is great! and i haven't given up on albers ;-)

It's truly a super helpful package for folks. It really lowers the
barrier to entry for a huge portion of R users.

parts:
With coord_quickmap() a rectangle is still a rectangle; with
coord_map() it might not be.
Hadley
